the large organic cation, TBA+, produces a unique reduced conductance state in the purified sheep SR Ca2+ release (RyR1) channel when present at its cytoplasmic (N)-face.

1) large organic cations block the Ca2+ channel to a level indistinguishable from its closed state; and 2) these cations are more effective blockers following ryanodine-induced modification, which suggests a structural change in a vestibule that reduces the capture area for blocking ions.

In summary, our research is concerned with
the molecular mechanism by which ryanodine modifies Ca2+ release from the sarcoplasmic (endoplasmic) reticulum of muscle cells.
the mechanism of the action of the plant alkaloid ryanodine on the Ca2+ channel of the sarcoplasmic/endoplasmic reticular membranes.
the structure and function of the ryanodin receptor Ca2+ release channels in cardiac muscle sarcoplasmic vesicles.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
TBA+ and other large organic cations are probes of the nature of the ryanodin modification of the sheep cardiac sarcopasmic reticulium Ca2+ release.
the large cations TBA+, tetrapentylammonium and QX314 block the Ca2+ channel by entering wide vestibules at the cytoplamic face of the channel and blocking conduction by partial occlusion.
the organic cations TBA+ and QX314 probe a vestibule of the Ca2+ channel, and that this vestibule is altered by ryanodine.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

ryanodine modifies the Ca2+ channel in such a way that it is more sensitive to the presence of large impermeant cations at the cytoplASMIC face of the channel, which we have interpreted as a consequence of a reduction in the size of the cytoplASMic vestibule.

TBA+ and other impermeant organic blocking cations are useful probes to study the conduction pathway and the vestibules of the cardiac Ca2+ release channels, and that the ryanoid receptor site is located in the vestibule at the cytoplamic face of the channel.
the ryanoidine-modified Ca2+ release channels of the sheep cardiac sarclemma are less permeable and less susceptible to block by organic cations than are the native channels.
The main takeaway from our work is that
large organic cations are useful for probing the nature of ryaodine modification in cardiac SR Ca2+ release channels.

the ryanoid binding site is located in a region of the channel that is accessible to the large impermeable organic cations, and that ryanodine modifies the channel to a state in which it is blocked by these cations.
the Ca2+ channel is not a simple cylinder with a central ion conduction pathway.
